messages.content:
Assign the three-character ICD-10-AM principal diagnosis category. Here are worked examples, then the case to code.

Example 1
Hospital course: A 72-year-old man with a 50 pack-year smoking history was admitted with three days of worsening breathlessness and purulent sputum. Spirometry showed an FEV1/FVC ratio of 0.52. He was treated with nebulised bronchodilators, oral prednisolone and antibiotics for an infective exacerbation of his long-standing airflow limitation.
Answer: J44

Example 2
Hospital course: A 58-year-old man presented with crushing central chest pain radiating to the jaw. The electrocardiogram showed ST elevation in the anterior leads and high-sensitivity troponin rose from 40 to 2100 ng/L. He underwent primary percutaneous coronary intervention with a stent to the proximal left anterior descending artery.
Answer: I21

Example 3
Hospital course: A 34-year-old woman presented with fever, rigors, dysuria and right flank tenderness. Urine microscopy showed pyuria and culture grew Escherichia coli. Computed tomography showed a swollen right kidney with no abscess. She improved on intravenous ceftriaxone.
Answer: N10

Example 4
Hospital course: An 81-year-old woman was brought in after a fall at home. She could not weight-bear and the right leg was shortened and externally rotated. A pelvic radiograph showed a displaced subcapital fracture of the right femoral neck. She underwent hemiarthroplasty on day one.
Answer: S72

Example 5
Hospital course: A 19-year-old man presented with 18 hours of periumbilical pain that migrated to the right iliac fossa, with anorexia and a low-grade fever. There was guarding at McBurney's point and the white cell count was 15.2. Laparoscopy confirmed an inflamed, non-perforated appendix.
Answer: K35

Example 6
Hospital course: A 64-year-old woman with a history of oestrogen-receptor-positive breast carcinoma treated five years earlier presented with progressive thoracic back pain. Magnetic resonance imaging showed deposits in T7 and T9 with no cord compression. Biopsy confirmed deposits of breast origin and she received palliative radiotherapy to the spine.
Answer: C79

Hospital course:
Discharge Summary:

Patient Name: ____
Date of Admission: ____
Date of Discharge: ____
Primary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Secondary Diagnosis: [diagnosis section withheld]
Hospital Course:
The patient was admitted to our facility on ____, exhibiting symptoms of tachycardia and acute kidney injury. It was later determined that the patient had ingested multiple foreign bodies. Treatment interventions included intravenous lorazepam and emergency laparotomy to remove all the packets. Postoperatively, the patient was transferred to the ICU where he remained for a total of one night before being transferred to ward level care. Pain management was achieved with a patient controlled analgesia (PCA) infusion pump, and the patient was extubated on day 1 postoperatively. The patient had a slow postoperative recovery mainly due to pain and limited oral fluid intake. He was discharged on day 10 back to police custody and returned once a week later for a dressing change.

Course of Treatment:
The course of treatment for this patient focused on the removal of the ingested foreign bodies through an emergency laparotomy. The patient was transferred to the ICU postoperatively and was managed with a patient controlled analgesia (PCA) infusion pump to manage pain.

Medications:
A detailed list of medications administered during the patient's hospitalization is not included in this summary.

Follow-up:
The patient was discharged on day 10 back to police custody and returned once a week later for a dressing change. No further follow-up was scheduled upon the patient's discharge.

Answer with the three-character category only.

text:
**T40**

This reads as body packing, where a person swallows drug packets, and the packets were removed at emergency laparotomy. Tachycardia and acute kidney injury treated with intravenous lorazepam point to drug toxicity from leaking packets. When packets cause poisoning, the poisoning is sequenced as the principal diagnosis ahead of the foreign body.

The summary never names the drug. I have assumed cocaine because it is the most commonly packed stimulant, which gives T40 (T40.5 at full code). If the drug were an amphetamine-type stimulant, the category would be T43 instead. If documentation showed no toxicity, the principal would be the foreign body in the alimentary tract, T18.
